Definition: Esav, a son of Isaac, including his posterity
BiblicalUsage: ʻÊsâv — Esau — was the elder twin of Isaac and Rebekah, a man of the field who sold his birthright for a meal of lentils. He comes back into the story when Jacob meets him again on the way home, and his descendants become the Edomites. His fuller story is on his People profile.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Esau matters because he is the warning in the family: a birthright thrown away for one meal. I hold that his tears afterward, when no repentance could undo it, are the soberest verses in Genesis.
